WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.ID,
        p.SEX,
        AVG(l.ALB) - AVG(l.TP) AS alb_minus_tp,
        AVG(l.APTT - l.PT) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
), sex_averages AS (
    SELECT
        SEX,
        AVG(alb_minus_tp) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
        AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM patient_averages
    GROUP BY SEX
), overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS mean_aptt_minus_pt
    FROM sex_averages
)
SELECT
    AVG(s.avg_alb_minus_tp) AS avg_alb_minus_tp,
    AVG(s.avg_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt,
    AVG(s.avg_aptt_minus_pt - m.mean_aptt_minus_pt) AS avg_excess_over_mean
FROM sex_averages AS s
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS m
WHERE s.avg_aptt_minus_pt > m.mean_aptt_minus_pt;

assumptions.assumption: Patient and sex averages include patients with linked laboratory records; each patient's ALB and TP means use their own non-missing values, while the mean per-test APTT − PT includes only tests where both values are present. Sex groups with no non-missing patient APTT − PT average do not contribute to the sex-level mean.
